scope: Rules fixed before new engine output is inspected. Constructed related task families, not independently sampled games or novice evaluation.

cases.human_task: A normal bishop move leaves the attacked e4 pawn without support. Read the actual first response and compare how the selected alternative handles the pawn; do not invent a forced loss.
The f3 pawn already supports e4. A defended pawn capture is not an unanswered undefended attack; preserve any real recapture and avoid judging the move from attack count alone.
Nc3 adds current support to the attacked e4 pawn. Several useful choices can exist; the alternative and its response determine the appropriate comment.
The f6 knight is pinned to its king by the f1 rook. Geometric contact does not establish a legal Nxe4 threat or a defensive failure.
Two initially attacked pawns on e5 and h4 require a complete comparison. Do not silently choose one arbitrary duty or hide the other actual capture.

Re1 supports e4 but the immediate Rxf6 opportunity takes a queen for a rook if the recorded Rxf6 follows. State the observed opportunity and its cost; do not assert that one PV proves forcing or compensation.
Ordinary development with existing support on both central pawns. Let multiple sound moves retain adequate purposes; do not manufacture an undefended-pawn failure.
A natural queen capture can lose that queen to Nxe4 and a further recapture. Root capture prices must remain complete, with the actual move judged before the alternative.
